doc: Application name must be topological_offset.
Input mesh, .msh: a triangle or a tetrahedral mesh. The two pipelines are the same algorithm one dimension apart and read every key below the same way.
Output file name (without extension).
Directory where the input files are located. This is injected by the application and should not be set by the user.
Boolean expression for input simplicial complex to offset. If a single tag (ie 'tag_0') is given, single body mode is used.
Tags to add to elements in the resulting offset region.
A tag.
Set of tags that will not be overwritten by the offset.
A tag.
Only relevant for single body mode. Whether to create offset inside body
Only relevant for single body mode. Whether to create offset outside body
Target offset distance relative to bounding box of mesh.
Target distance for offset. If < 0, the relative target distance is used to compute this one.

If true, a run that finishes without meeting the convergence criteria raises an error instead of logging a warning. Default false: a non-converged offset is still a usable one, and the warnings already name which criterion failed. Integration tests set it true so a convergence regression fails the run rather than passing with a warning.

Run the optimization (optimize_offset: pre-loop setup, the loop's turns, the final pass and the convergence verdict) after the offset is constructed. Default true. false: the run stops at the constructed offset -- the simplicial embedding, the marching and the tag assignment still run -- and writes it as the result. The constructed band lies on the background mesh's own cell boundaries, so its distance to the input complex is set by the input mesh's resolution, not by target_distance; the report then carries converged = false and no optimization metrics, and throw_on_nonconvergence is not consulted.

Half-width, relative to the bounding box diagonal, of the envelope that holds the held surfaces during optimization; any operation that would push a held face outside it is rejected, and a held vertex is smoothed toward it. 3D: ONE envelope around every held face, built once after the simplicial embedding, before the repulsion and the march: the domain wall, and the input complex's boundary when deform_others is true, or every region boundary when it is false (see deform_others). The offset surface is never in it. 2D: one tube per region tag, as before. Ignored if envelope_size >= 0.
Absolute half-width of the envelope that holds the held surfaces (see envelope_size_rel). If < 0, computed from envelope_size_rel.

Which field defines the offset, and so what the front is placed on, what the criterion measures and what the sizing field refines by. 'smooth' is the offset geometric contact potential Phi, with the front on the level set Phi = c: C^2, analytic derivatives, and a level set that bulges outward at reentrant features, so it is a smoothed offset rather than the exact one. 'euclidean' (the default) is the exact distance to the input complex, which makes the residual exact but introduces a gradient discontinuity across the medial axis and a crease at every reentrant feature that no refinement resolves; offset_dhat_factor and the outside-the-support guard stop meaning anything, since it has no compact support.

Support radius of the smooth offset potential, as a multiple of target_distance. Must be > 1. The offset level set lies strictly inside the support; a band vertex that leaves the support is a hard error.

THE convergence epsilon, as an ABSOLUTE length in model units; < 0 (the default) means use front_conv_rel instead. Absolute-or-relative exactly as envelope_size / envelope_size_rel, and against the same reference, the bounding box diagonal -- deliberately NOT a fraction of target_distance, so changing the offset distance no longer silently changes the accuracy. Startup refuses a value above target_distance: an epsilon coarser than the offset it measures decides nothing, since every front face then reads as resolved from the first turn. THIS IS THE ONLY BAR, in 2D and 3D. The measure it gates is one quantity everywhere: over a face's stencil_order stencil (in 2D a front chord's), the ROOT MEAN SQUARE of the distance to the level set along the field, over target_distance (for 'euclidean' the relative error (Phi - c)/c = (d - target_distance)/target_distance; for 'smooth' the root of Phi = c along grad Phi, since there (Phi - c)/c is not a length and read 3.44x the distance error at offset_dhat_factor 2), taken as a length. A face is resolved when that RMS is <= front_conv, i.e. when the MEAN SQUARED relative error is <= (front_conv/target_distance)^2; a vertex is placed when the same measure at the vertex alone -- the order-0 stencil -- is within it. So the vertex measure and the face measure are ONE measure at two sample counts, which is why vertex_conv and sag_conv, which split them apart on 2026-09-23, no longer exist. The offset surface debug field f_err reports the same number. The front smoothing objective (StencilEnergy3D, StencilEnergy2D) has the same zero set but, under 'smooth', charges the field error (Phi - c)/c rather than this distance: about 3.44x it at offset_dhat_factor 2. WHAT THE LOOP EXITS ON is set by front_measure: under the default 'vertex_ring', every front vertex's ring measure (the RMS of its offset faces' measures, every face weighted equally) within the bar; under 'face', the rule of 2026-09-25, every offset face's measure within the bar. Either way nothing may be unmeasurable, the single-point vertex measure is a diagnostic that decides nothing about termination, and an element over the bar that refinement cannot take (the sizing floor) blocks the exit and is named in a warning every turn it exists. 2D runs the same criterion on its front chords (offset edges in place of offset faces).

THE convergence epsilon as a fraction of the BOUNDING BOX DIAGONAL, used when front_conv is < 0. The default 2.5e-4 is the old front_conv_rel default 0.025 times the default target_distance_rel 0.01, so a fully default run keeps the accuracy it has always had; at any other target_distance the default accuracy now differs from the pre-2026-09-23 behaviour, which is the point of referencing the box rather than the offset. See front_conv for what the bar actually gates.

Order of the sampling stencil on an offset-surface face (3D) or front chord (2D). It sets BOTH the convergence measure and the front smoothing energy, which sample the same points. Order 0 is the 3 CORNERS alone, so the measure is exactly the three vertices' own placement error. Order k >= 1 is the vertices of the triangle subdivided k-1 times by 4-way midpoint refinement, plus the centroid of each of its 4^(k-1) sub-triangles: with n = 2^(k-1) segments per side that is (n+1)(n+2)/2 + n^2 points, i.e. 4 at order 1 (the corners and the centroid), 10 at order 2 (the corners, the 3 edge midpoints and the 4 sub-triangle centroids), 31 at order 3, 109 at order 4. On a 2D chord the same rule one dimension down: order 0 is the 2 ENDS alone, order k >= 1 the vertices of the chord cut into 2^(k-1) pieces plus the midpoint of each piece, i.e. 3, 5, 9, 17 points. THE CORNERS ARE IN THE STENCIL, unlike the strictly interior lattice sag_num_samples used, and they have to be: the quantity sampled is a distance to the level set, which at a corner is that vertex's own placement error rather than the identically-zero interpolation error the old measure saw there. That is what lets one stencil replace the separate vertex and sag criteria. COST: every sample is a Phi value and, in the smoothing energy, a gradient too, so the order is paid in the operations' energy rules (TopoOffsetTetMesh::tet_energy(), TopoOffsetTriMesh::tri_energy()) and in every smoothing solve as well as in the criterion -- 4 points at the default against 6 for the old default.

Which measure the loop exits on and refines by, in 3D and in 2D. 'vertex_ring' (the default): at each front vertex v the RING MEASURE r_v = sqrt((1/n_v) sum_f m_f^2), over the n_v offset faces f incident to v whose three corners are front vertices, every face weighted equally, m_f the face measure, the root of face_offset_term() (the RMS over the face's stencil_order stencil of the distance to the level set along the field over target_distance -- for 'euclidean' the relative error (Phi - c)/c -- over the bar front_conv / target_distance). m_f^2 is the term the per-tet energy (TopoOffsetTetMesh::tet_energy()) adds to the face's band cell, which is why there is no area in it. The loop exits when every ring measure is within the bar and nothing is unmeasurable; a vertex with an unmeasurable incident face has no ring measure and blocks the exit. The face and vertex measures are then reported as diagnostics. The halving lowers the sizing scalar at each vertex whose ring measure is over the bar, that vertex alone, under the same floor (max of min_sizing_scalar and min_edge_length / l); a vertex over the bar already at the floor blocks the exit and is named by the [sizing floor] warning. The chord rule is not read in this mode. The operations do not compare this measure: since 2026-09-28 the collapse, the swaps and the front smoother compare the per-tet energy (TopoOffsetTetMesh::tet_energy()), whose front terms are these m_f^2 (until then an ops guard compared the ring measure before against after). The front smoother's offset term is the sum of the same faces' m_f^2, n_v r_v^2, every face weighing 1. From 2026-09-25 to 2026-09-28 both this measure and the smoother weighted each face by its area (A_f, and A_f / A_mean in the smoother) so that the two agreed; they now agree unweighted, as the per-tet energy has no area in it. In 2D the same criterion runs on the front chords: r_v = sqrt((1/n_v) sum_e m_e^2) over the n_v front chords e incident to v, m_e the chord measure (the root of edge_offset_term()), every chord weighted equally, with the same exit and the same per-vertex halving; 2D's operations compare the per-cell energy TopoOffsetTriMesh::tri_energy() and its front smoother minimises StencilEnergy2D, the same chords' m_e^2. 'face': the rule of 2026-09-25, kept for comparison. The loop exits when every offset face's (2D: chord's) measure is within the bar and nothing is unmeasurable; the halving lowers the sizing scalar at the corners of every face over the bar whose chord rule still has a target below its corners' scalars. Why the ring measure: the smoother minimises a sum over each vertex's ring while the face exit and refinement are per face, and the two disagree at the margin. Measured on the deliverable cube at target_distance_rel 1e-3 / front_conv_rel 1e-5 under 'face', turns 12-15: the loop never exits because a handful of faces end each turn at 1.00 to 1.19 times the bar, the smoothing having pushed faces from 0.99 to just over the bar while lowering the ring they belong to. On the cube at target_distance_rel 1e-2 / front_conv_rel 1e-4 (EXPERIMENTAL_nonoverlapping_gates true, interleaved_smoothing false, 2 smoothing passes, no alignment term, serial), measured with the area weights and before the per-tet energy: 'vertex_ring' exits after 7 turns with max AMIPS 8.784 and 20724 front faces, 60 of them over the bar (the largest 1.355x) while every ring measure is within it (the largest 0.963x); 'face' exits after 7 turns with max AMIPS 7.814 and 23476 front faces. The debug frames carry the ring measure as point data, front_ring_ratio, in both modes (2D: on the _front.vtu chord mesh).
Execute the marching in decreasing order of edge length. Increases run time, may increase output mesh quality.

In (0, 1). The marching's sphere trace stops at the first point where |d(x) - D| <= this x D, D being the distance the march traces to (target_distance, or half the maximum marchable distance under construction_mode max_marchable_fallback); the placed vertex is that close to that level set along the edge. Smaller is tighter and takes more steps (each step is longer than the tolerance, so at most edge length / (this x D) per edge).

How the marching constructs the offset. Construction first measures the maximum marchable distance, the smallest distance from the input complex of the outer end of any marched edge (an edge with one end in the input complex and the other in the background). Every marched edge's inner end is on the complex, so the level set d = D crosses every marched edge for every D up to that distance. If target_distance is below it, every marched edge is split where d(x) = target_distance, found by sphere tracing from the complex end (to within sphere_trace_target_rel_tol). Otherwise: 'max_marchable_fallback' (the default) traces every marched edge to half the maximum marchable distance instead; 'midpoint_fallback' splits every marched edge at its midpoint. Either way target_distance itself is not changed: the optimization carries the offset surface out to it. Both dimensions.

Default true, 2D and 3D. Construction measures the maximum marchable distance, the smallest distance from the input complex of the outer end of any marched edge (the largest target every marched edge can be traced to). If target_distance is below it, the init_optimize loop is not done: the offset is marched to the target and the loop runs with refinement as usual, and the log says so. If target_distance is not below it, every marched edge is split as construction_mode says (the default traces it to half the maximum marchable distance; midpoint_fallback splits it at its midpoint), the loop first converges under stencil_order with no refinement (the sizing field left as it is), without the final pass, and then the ordinary loop converges under the same stencil_order with its refinement, final pass and verdict. target_distance is never changed. The no-refinement loop's debug frames are led by i.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-02), 2D and 3D. The stencil_order of the init_optimize loop alone -- its front smoothing energy, its operations' energy rules and its exit test; the loop with refinement after it uses stencil_order. -1 (the default) uses stencil_order in both loops, as before. Why: without refinement the faces keep the base edge length, so a measure that samples inside the faces (order >= 1) cannot be met where the level set curves, and the loop runs to max_rounds -- on the one-slot model (offset-runs/slot_repro/slot_small.msh) at the default, every front vertex was over the bar at the end of all 7 init turns. Order 0 samples the corners alone, each front vertex's own placement error, which does not depend on the face size.

2D and 3D. At most this many smoothing passes between the simplicial embedding and the march, so that the march can trace to target_distance itself. The march traces every marched edge (one end in the input complex, the other not) to target_distance only if every outer end is farther than it (the maximum marchable distance, see construction_mode); otherwise it falls back. The repulsion vertices are those outer ends -- the one ring of the input complex's vertices minus the complex -- that no input envelope holds. One per-tet energy holds before the march: w AMIPS^3 (2D: w AMIPS, the 2D engine's quality; w = offset_amips_weight, as the front) plus, for each corner v of the cell (2D: face) that is a repulsion vertex joined in that cell to the input complex by a marched edge, O(v) = (max(0, 2 delta - d(v)) / front_conv)^2, delta = target_distance, d the Euclidean distance to the input complex. O is one-sided, so it pushes a vertex out and never pulls one in, and its target is 2 delta so that the march at delta splits each edge with room to spare (the construction's own fallback, half the maximum marchable distance, run backwards). Every vertex is smoothed against the sum of that energy over its ring, so a repulsion vertex's O(v) counts once for every ring cell that carries it; every other vertex is smoothed as in the loop (envelopes, offset_smooth_veto on the energy's max). Under offset_front_smooth_veto a repulsion move may not raise the max of the energy over its ring. The passes stop as soon as every outer end is farther than delta + front_conv, i.e. outside the tolerance band. Each pass logs the maximum marchable distance, the outer ends within delta + front_conv, delta and 2 delta, and the max AMIPS; with debug_output a frame repulsion_<k> follows each pass. 0 (the default) = off: no pass, no frame, no log line.

2D and 3D. After the repulsion_smoothing_passes (if any) and before the march, at most this many rounds of the loop's operations: split, collapse and swap, each followed by its smoothing passes, shaped as interleaved_smoothing says (adaptive smoothing is not used). No refinement: the sizing field is never lowered, so every operation aims at the base edge length. No split of a marched edge (one end in the input complex): its midpoint would be a new outer end nearer the input. The collapses and swaps compare the per-tet energy of repulsion_smoothing_passes, repulsion terms included, as the loop's rules compare its energy. The input complex stays simplicially embedded, as the march needs it: a collapse or swap that would leave a cell off the complex whose complex vertices span an edge or face off the complex is refused. After every operation pass the construction labels are recomputed from the region tags, and the repulsion vertices follow the operations. Single-body offset_in or offset_out only (the embedding test reads the complex off the cells' labels); other selections, and in 2D a curve group, are refused with an error. The rounds stop as soon as every outer end is farther than target_distance + front_conv. Each round logs its operations' outcomes ([ops accounting], [swap reject], 3D only: the 2D engine has neither; the embedding refusals, which those counters have no name for, are counted on the round's own line), the maximum marchable distance and the max AMIPS; with debug_output a frame repulsion_round_<k> follows each round. The embedding test reads cells beyond an operation's lock, so run the rounds with num_threads 0. 0 (the default) = off.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-07), with EXPERIMENTAL_growth_targets only (refused otherwise). The construction target as a fraction of target_distance, in (0, the first growth target]; construction (repulsion, the march, init_optimize when the march falls back) runs there instead of at the first growth target, and the field is rebuilt at the first growth target before the push (EXPERIMENTAL_growth_push) or stage 1. 0 (the default) = construction at the first growth target. Why: on Thingi10K 100026 (target_distance_rel 5e-3) the band cells that cover a slot's mid-plane at its ends reach 3.6 x the construction target along the slot -- 0.36 at 0.1 delta, 1.77 at 0.5 delta, against the end cap's own reach of 1 x the target -- because the march places their front corners at the target's distance along fixed background edges running across and along the slot.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-07), with EXPERIMENTAL_growth_targets only (refused otherwise). Before stage 1: smoothing blocks alone at the first growth target -- no split, collapse or swap, no refinement, so the cells stay the ones construction made -- each block the one every operation group of the loop is followed by (interleaved_smoothing_passes or num_smoothing_passes passes, or adaptive smoothing), until every front vertex is placed (its own distance to the level set within front_conv) and none is unmeasurable. At most max_rounds blocks; a push that does not get there stops the run, as a stage does. Frames in push/ beside the output, labels led by p. Meant with EXPERIMENTAL_growth_construction below the first target: construct low, move the front without operations, then the stages. false (the default) = no push.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-08), 3D, front_measure "vertex_ring" only (refused otherwise). ONE global energy that every step of the loop descends: E' = sum over front faces of area(f) O(f) + (offset_amips_weight / front_conv) sum over tets of vol(t) AMIPS(t)^3 -- the discrete surface integral of e^2 = ((d - target_distance) / front_conv)^2 over the front plus the discrete volume integral of AMIPS^3, both converging under refinement; areas and volumes are the current ones. The per-tet energy is (w/eps) vol AMIPS^3 plus area(f) O(f) for the front face the tet carries. The front smoother minimises the part of E' at the vertex (coordinate descent, no veto); a non-front vertex minimises its ring's (w/eps) sum vol AMIPS^3 (no veto); a collapse or a swap is accepted when the SUM of the per-tet energy over the cells it changes does not rise (a swap: strictly falls), in place of TetWild's max rule, and the engine's early refusals on the AMIPS^3 bound are off. The exit's ring measure R(v) is area-weighted. Splits are unchanged. Why: a per-face sum of O(f) is not an integral (it grows with the face count) and rewards sliding a vertex toward lower error where the level set is out of reach; the area-weighted R(v) alone was not one energy. false (the default) = the per-tet energy and the max rules as before.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-08), 3D, one input region, offset_field "euclidean" only (refused otherwise, and with EXPERIMENTAL_integral_energy, EXPERIMENTAL_area_weighted_ring, EXPERIMENTAL_quadratic_stencil or EXPERIMENTAL_visible_distance). The front's offset term becomes the integral of e = (d - target_distance) / front_conv over the band region B: E = int_B e dV + offset_amips_weight * sum over tets of vol(t) AMIPS(t)^3, both volumes. int_B e dV is evaluated per band cell as its volume times the mean of e over its four corners and its centroid (exact where d is affine on the cell, i.e. one input face is nearest; second order where a kink or a curved d crosses it). Near the level set int_B e dV = (front_conv / 2) int_front e^2 dA, so the balance with AMIPS is the face term's, without the area term that rewards shrinking a front whose error cannot reach zero (the pressed front where target_distance exceeds half a slot's width). The front smoother minimises the vertex's part of E (no veto); a non-front vertex minimises its ring's w sum vol AMIPS^3 (no veto): E does not depend on interior vertices. A collapse is accepted when the max of w AMIPS^3 over the changed cells does not rise (as before) and the sum of the band-cell term over the changed band cells does not rise; a swap when that max strictly falls (the existing rule and gates) and that sum does not rise. Splits and the exit test are unchanged. false (the default) = the per-tet energy with the face term, as before.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-08), 3D, a diagnostic. The offset loop halves no sizing scalar: the exit criterion's refinable vertices or faces are logged and left as they are. false (the default) = refinement as configured.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-08), 3D, a diagnostic. The offset loop does not exit on its criterion: every loop runs max_rounds turns, and the criterion's numbers are still logged each turn. Under growth stages a stage therefore never converges, so the run stops after stage 1. Why: to watch the energy across operations and turns (under EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_energy every debug frame appends its index, label and the energy's two parts to <output>_energy.txt). false (the default) = the loop exits when its criterion holds.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-08), needs EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_energy. The band-volume integrand's divisor: "front_conv" integrates (d - target_distance) / front_conv, "target_distance" integrates (d - target_distance) / target_distance. At a fixed target the two differ by the constant factor target_distance / front_conv, i.e. by the AMIPS term's effective weight.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-08), needs EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_energy. The rule that integrates the band-volume integrand over one band cell: "five_point" = volume times the mean over the cell's four corners and its centroid; "centroid" = volume times the value at the centroid; "corner_bound" = volume times the min, over candidate input triangles P, of the mean of (d_P - target_distance)/target_distance over the cell's four corners, d_P the distance to triangle P alone (candidates: the nearest triangle of each corner, and the triangle the cell stored at the last split pass, which split children inherit). corner_bound is an upper bound on the exact integral (d <= d_P, and the convex d_P lies below its linear interpolant) and no split raises it (a child can use its parent's triangle, whose finer interpolant lies lower); it needs an input complex of triangles only. All three are exact where the distance is affine on the cell. Measured on the one-slot model (stage 1, cells about 10x target_distance): corners on the input read (d - delta)/delta = -1 whatever the cell's interior is, so five_point read a band tet with all four corners on the input as -1.57 against a dense +4.83 (centroid alone +5.68), and over the band -41.0 against a dense +13.1 (centroid alone +24.6).

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-08), needs EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_energy. The AMIPS term of the energy is offset_amips_weight * sum over tets of vol (AMIPS / stop_energy)^3, about 1 for a cell at the stop energy, instead of offset_amips_weight * sum vol AMIPS^3. The max rules compare AMIPS and are unaffected.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-08), needs EXPERIMENTAL_band_volume_energy. Every operation judges by the global energy E alone. A collapse is accepted when the sum of E's per-cell terms (the AMIPS term, plus the band-volume term of a band cell) over the cells it changes does not rise, a swap when that sum strictly falls -- including the 4-4 / 5-6 case search and the face swap's gate, which score candidate cells by the same sum; the AMIPS max rules and the engine's early refusals on the AMIPS bound are off. Every vertex's smoothing objective is its part of E: a vertex off the front also carries the band-volume term of its band cells, since the cell rule depends on it where d is not affine. Splits stay independent of the energy.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-08), 3D, stencil_order >= 1 only (refused otherwise). O(f), the face's mean of e^2 over its stencil, weighs the stencil points by the quadrature rule exact for quadratics on each sub-triangle (corners 1/12, centroid 3/4, composed over the sub-triangles) instead of equally, so O(f) is the face's exact mean of e^2 whenever e is affine on each sub-triangle. One definition, so everything that reads O(f) changes with it: tet_energy(), the front smoother, the ring measure and the face measures; the remainder W is the same weighted least-squares fit. Why: under EXPERIMENTAL_area_weighted_ring the one-slot model at stage 9 still had 8-23 vertices per turn sliding along the pressed front where e rises steeply along it; equal weights do not integrate e^2's quadratic part exactly. false (the default) = equal weights.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-08), 3D, front_measure "vertex_ring" only (refused otherwise). The ring measure becomes the mean of O(f) over a front vertex's faces weighted by their areas, R(v)^2 = sum area(f) O(f) / sum area(f) (W(v) likewise, of the faces' remainders), and the front smoother minimises w AMIPS^3 / n + R(v)^2, n the faces at the vertex -- the same objective as before up to the constant n, with R(v)^2 area-weighted and the areas taken at the iterate (differentiated). Why: with every face weighing 1, a vertex sliding within a front whose error cannot reach 0 moves its samples toward lower error at no cost to the surface; on the one-slot model at targets above half the slot width, the pressed front above and below the plate (where the distance grows along the front toward its edge) slid outward every pass, collapses removed the vertices at the edge and splits refilled it, and the exit's own-change test failed at 383-560 vertices per turn. Measured at stage 9: sliding 0.02 outward lowered the unweighted sum at 514 of 517 failing vertices, the area-weighted one at 225. tet_energy() is unchanged (its rules compare maxima). false (the default) = every face weighs 1.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-07), 3D, front_measure "vertex_ring" and stencil_order >= 1 only (refused otherwise). With e = (d - target_distance) / front_conv at the stencil samples, a front face's remainder is the mean over its samples of (e - L)^2, L the least-squares function linear on the face (order 1: (3/16) b^2, b the centroid's e minus the mean of the corners'), and W(v) is the mean over v's faces. Per front vertex v, in order: R(v) <= 1 passes; W(v) > 1 fails and halves v's sizing scalar; otherwise v passes when its front solve in the turn's last operation group (the last smoothing passes) changed its own e by at most 1, a refused move counting as no change (the level set is out of reach there), else it fails without refinement and is left to smoothing. Why: for target_distance above half a slot's width the loop keeps the slot's hole open, so the front in the slot stays (target_distance - width/2) / front_conv over the bar on any mesh, and refining on R or on the variance of e over the ring refines a planar front where only the distance rising along it varies (slot_small, width 2.5, target 1.35: 86-99.5% of that variance linear). false (the default) = the ring measure alone.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-07), 3D, euclidean field, front_measure "vertex_ring", serial (num_threads 0), one input region, an input with triangles (refused otherwise). From the first loop turn on (the march keeps the euclidean distance), every reading of the field at a point of the front -- the face terms of the per-tet energy and the exit, the front smoother, the vertex measures, the frames -- uses d_vis: the distance to the nearest input point q such that the segment from the point to q lies in closed band cells, except that it may end in input cells (the mesh's input cells stand off the input triangles by up to the input envelope) and must reach a triangle bounding the solid from its outer side. Where the segment to the nearest input point stays in the band, d_vis is the euclidean distance. Where it does not -- a front vertex of one side of a slot past the slot's midline is nearest the other wall through cells that are not band -- d_vis measures to the wall the point's band is attached to, so the pull no longer reverses at the midline. Exact: orientation predicates and rationals on the positions as given. Two assumptions, each counted per turn in the log ([visible distance]): a point that sees no input point takes the euclidean distance; a triangle closer than every point proven visible whose nearest point among the directions into the band is hidden further along the segment (part of it may still be visible) gives that point's distance, a lower bound of d_vis -- the log reports the largest gap to the nearest point proven visible, the most the value can be off. Derivatives at a foot found through the directions into the band ignore the motion of those directions with a moving vertex. A walk that cannot be completed stops the run with a message. The operations keep their local rule (the energy over the cells they change), although a face's d_vis also depends on the cells its segments pass through, so an operation can change the energy of a face outside them. false (the default) = the euclidean distance.
A target as a fraction of target_distance.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-06), 3D only (2D refuses a non-empty list). Grows the offset to target_distance (delta) through the listed targets, given as fractions of delta, strictly increasing, in (0, 1], the last exactly 1 (anything else is refused at startup); e.g. [0.5, 0.75, 1] or [0.1, 0.2, ..., 1]. Stage k works at target growth_targets[k-1] x delta under the configured front_conv, the same absolute length at every stage. Construction (repulsion, the march, init_optimize when the march falls back) runs at the first target. Stages before the last run the loop under stencil_order, with refinement, until it converges, without the final pass or the verdict; the field is rebuilt at each new target. The last stage is the ordinary loop at delta, with its final pass and verdict. Everything else stays as configured: offset_envelope, envelope_size, the base edge length, min_edge_length and the sizing floor (absolute lengths fixed when the parameters are read), and the sizing field carries over from stage to stage (nothing raises it). A stage before the last that does not converge within max_rounds turns stops the run: the later stages are not run, and the verdict reports the mesh as that stage left it, against that stage's target. With debug_output every stage's frames are a series of their own in stage_<k>/ beside the output (own <output>_frames.txt and .pvd files, opening with a stage_start frame of the stage's starting mesh); the frames up to construction stay beside the output. Labels of stages before the last are led by g<k>. Why: on the one-slot model the first smoothing pass at delta carries front vertices across the slot (offset-runs/sublevel/span_trace); small steps keep every move a fraction of delta. Measured with [0.1, 0.2, ..., 1] at stencil_order 1 and front_conv 1% of delta (offset-runs/growth): the one-slot model at widths 2.2 (cap 10), 2.5 and 3.0 and the 36-long slot converge with no band cell on the slot's mid-plane at any stage; at stencil_order 0 every stage converges in 1-2 turns while the first collapse lets the band cover the mid-plane (order 0 does not see a face spanning the gap). Empty (the default) = off; [1] is the same as off.

EXPERIMENTAL (2026-10-07), 3D, euclidean offset_field only, needs repulsion_rounds > 0. The repulsion also refines, before the march, where the front the march would cut fails the loop's own face measure. At every report (before the passes, after each pass and each round) the front at target_distance (the construction target) is predicted: on every marched edge the split point is the sphere trace's, the point the march creates; in every cell with a marched edge these points bound the cell's front piece, a triangle, or a quad measured in both triangulations because the march's split order picks its diagonal; each triangle is measured by the loop's face measure (face_offset_term(): stencil_order, front_conv). The sizing scalar is halved, and graded, at the corners of every cell whose piece is over the bar, as the loop halves. The rounds' split pass realizes it, refusing marched edges as always, so the refinement runs along the input and the outer ends and never across the future band; the rounds have no collapse group; the repulsion term keeps the outer ends beyond target_distance. The passes and rounds stop once every outer end is beyond target_distance + front_conv AND no predicted piece is over the bar (or none is unmeasurable). The lowered sizing field carries into the loop. Why: on Thingi10K 100026 the slot-end band cells that cover a slot's mid-plane reach 3.6 x the construction target along the slot, whatever the target, because the march's split points slide along fixed background edges running across and along the slot; refining after the march splits those cells' front edges, whose midpoints land in the gap. false (the default) = the rounds as before.

EXPERIMENTAL, default false pending more runs. Separates the two edge-length gates so that a split can never hand the collapse pass its own halves. Both passes measure the same ratio r = L / (l x the mean of the two endpoints' sizing scalars): the split pass fires when r > 4/3 (splitting_l2 = (4/3 l)^2) and the collapse pass offers a candidate when r < 4/5 (collapsing_l2 = (4/5 l)^2). The two windows overlap, so an edge with 4/3 < r < 8/5 is split into two halves of ratio r/2 < 4/5, which the collapse pass in the same turn merges back into the edge that was just split. With this key true, splitting_l2 becomes (8/5 l)^2 -- exactly twice the collapse gate -- and collapsing_l2 is unchanged, so every half a split produces has ratio at or above 4/5 and is never a collapse candidate. Nothing else changes: a split is still never refused on quality, this is a length rule alone. Measured on the deliverable cube at target_distance_rel 1e-2 / front_conv_rel 1e-4 without the alignment term: 29068 of 35865 split candidates at the end of turn 7 (81%) lay in the 4/3 to 8/5 band, and turns 6, 7 and 8 each performed about 36k splits and 29k collapses while refinement halved the sizing scalar at 0 vertices. With the key on: operations in the last turn 66826 -> 19263, turns 8 -> 7, wall 223 -> 126 s, final max AMIPS 8.69 -> 10.64, front faces 25816 -> 21042, both runs meeting the same convergence test. false, the default, keeps the TetWild gates.
After performing offset, check if offset region is manifold
Save .vtu of output mesh

Samples per side of the grid the smooth offset potential is written on, as <output>_phi.vtu, for the viewer. 0 disables it. The grid is the plane through the box centre normal to the box's shortest extent (the whole domain when the domain is planar). Carries phi, phi_residual_length and euclidean_distance per vertex; warp by phi to see the field as a height surface.

Write debug VTU frames of the evolving mesh, in both dimensions: one frame after every operation pass and every smoothing pass, as sequential <output>_NNNNN.vtu files so ParaView loads them as one time series, plus <output>_frames.txt carrying one 'NNNNN<tab>r<turn><phase><pass>_<op>' line per frame, which the viewer scripts read for their labels. Expect hundreds of frames on a real model; observational only, the frames cannot change the run.
Logs are not just printed on the terminal but also saved in this file.
A JSON file that stores information about the result and the method execution, e.g., runtime.

Mesh storage (connectivity and attributes) is preallocated to this factor times the live element count at init and at consolidation. Operations take fresh slots from that headroom and are retried once it is exhausted. Lower it for pure-decimation runs and raise it for aggressive refinement; the offset refines aggressively, so a run whose log carries [slots] warnings is dropping the very splits the criterion asked for.
Number of threads used for parallel execution (smoothing, edge collapse). 0 means single-threaded.

Smoothing passes after the ONE combined split+collapse+swap round when interleaved_smoothing is OFF (the default is ON since 2026-09-28) -- in the loop (3D since 2026-09-25, 2D since 2026-10-05; only when adaptive_smoothing is also off), and in the shared optimization loop, which in this component is the frozen-front finishing pass, 2D and 3D alike. The default turn is therefore split, collapse, swap, then 2 smoothing passes. Not read when interleaving is on: the count is then interleaved_smoothing_passes, everywhere. TriWild's key and TriWild's default.

Target edge length relative to the bounding box diagonal. Used to bound which edges edge collapse is allowed to touch (only edges shorter than 4/5 of this length are collapsed). Ignored if length >= 0.
Target edge length (absolute). If < 0, computed from length_rel.

Target AMIPS quality for the elements. Default 100, matching the tetwild component -- the frozen-front finishing pass is TriWild/TetWild and stops where they stop. Do not lower it far: a target the operation set cannot deliver turns the split pass into an unbounded refiner. Edge collapse will not push an already-on-target region's quality back above this.

Cap on the shared TriWild/TetWild loop, which now runs in exactly one place: the finishing pass that runs with the front frozen. The loop exits as soon as max AMIPS is under stop_energy, so this is an upper bound.

Half-width of the corridor the frozen-front final pass must keep the front inside (the loop holds the front to no envelope), as an ABSOLUTE length in model units; < 0 (the default) means use offset_envelope_rel instead. Absolute-or-relative exactly as envelope_size / envelope_size_rel. It is a leash, not an accuracy knob: front_conv sets the accuracy, and startup requires this to be <= front_conv, because a wider leash lets the operations dent the front past the resolution threshold and mint new refinable faces every turn. Tighter over-constrains the passes and starts refusing operations that were not straddling the boundary at all. It also feeds the derived sizing floor when min_edge_length_rel is negative, as this length expressed in units of target_distance.

Half-width of the corridor the frozen-front final pass must keep the front inside, as a fraction of the BOUNDING BOX DIAGONAL, used when offset_envelope is < 0. Built once, from the front as the loop left it, for the frozen-front final pass; the loop holds the front to no envelope. THE REFERENCE CHANGED on 2026-09-24: it was a fraction of target_distance. A fully default run is NOT unchanged -- the old default 0.025 x the default target_distance_rel 0.01 came to 2.5e-4 of the diagonal, and this default is 1e-4, so the leash is 2.5x TIGHTER at defaults and the operation passes are correspondingly more constrained. At other target distances it moves the other way: at target_distance_rel 1e-3 the old key gave 2.5e-5 of the diagonal where this gives 1e-4, a leash four times wider. See offset_envelope for what the corridor is and what startup requires of it.

Run split, collapse and swap as three separate rounds with `interleaved_smoothing_passes` smoothing passes after each, instead of one combined round followed by `num_smoothing_passes`. DEFAULT TRUE since 2026-09-28 (it was false from 2026-09-25, when the smoothing was 63% of a turn and 5 of its 6 passes near no-ops; the single energy, the exact Hessian and the relative gradient tolerance made a front solve 2-3 Newton iterations instead of 10). Measured on the cube with the single energy, mix vetos: serial target 1e-2 / tolerance 1e-4, combined 7 turns / 22396 faces / 215 s, interleaved 6 / 20102 / 203 s; 10 threads, combined 7-9 turns / 22260-25416 faces / 55-98 s, interleaved 6-7 / 19870-21186 / 60-75 s; 10 threads 1e-3 / 5e-5 (neither resolved in 10 turns), combined 95040 faces / 330 s, interleaved 75826 / 390 s. The gain is in the late turns: the front the exit test judges has been re-placed after every operation, so fewer vertices are over the bar and halved.

Smoothing passes after each operation group (split, collapse, swap) when interleaved_smoothing is on -- in the shared TriWild/TetWild loop (the frozen-front finishing pass) and in the loop. Default 2, against the shared engine's own 1: each smoothing pass is one placement sweep of the front, so at one pass per group the front contracts about half as fast for the same final result. In the loop this fixed count is only used when adaptive_smoothing is false.

The loop only, not the final pass. Run the smoothing after each operation group pass by pass until it has converged or stalled, instead of a fixed count: after the one combined group under interleaved_smoothing false in place of num_smoothing_passes, and after each of the three groups (split, collapse, swap) under true (the default) in place of interleaved_smoothing_passes. 2D and 3D alike. After every pass two things are measured against the positions before it. Front vertices (on the offset): the convergence ratio front_vertex_conv_ratio, the vertex's own relative error over the bar -- converged when its maximum is at or below 1, stalled when the maximum fell by less than adaptive_smoothing_stall_rel of its previous value, since a stalled front needs an operation and not another sweep. Background vertices: the step each vertex made divided by its target edge length s_v * l -- settled when the maximum is at or below adaptive_smoothing_step_rel. The group's smoothing stops when the front is converged or stalled AND the background has settled, or at adaptive_smoothing_max_passes. Front vertices whose ratio is not measurable (a non-finite residual) are counted and left out of the maximum.
Upper bound on the smoothing passes of one operation group under adaptive_smoothing; at least 1 pass always runs.

Under adaptive_smoothing the front counts as stalled when a pass lowered the maximum convergence ratio by less than this fraction of its value before the pass (0.1 = less than 10 percent). Never applied to the first pass of a group.
Under adaptive_smoothing the background counts as settled when no non-front vertex moved more than this fraction of its own target edge length s_v * l in the pass.

The loop only, not the final pass. true: before the first turn, run one smoothing block on the mesh as constructed -- the same block each operation group is followed by: num_smoothing_passes sweeps under interleaved_smoothing false and interleaved_smoothing_passes under true (the default), 2D and 3D alike; or the adaptive smoothing when adaptive_smoothing is on -- with the plastic rests stamped before it (2D: and the released-boundary tube refreshed after it), so the front is carried toward the level set once before the first split pass measures it. false (the default): the loop starts with turn 1's split pass on the constructed mesh.

Run the post-optimization coarsening pass, as TriWild and TetWild do. It trades elements for nothing but the guarantee that the result is still good, so topological_offset holds it to an absolute bar -- both AMIPS and the offset residual inside tolerance after each collapse -- rather than the non-degrading bar the main loop uses. Off by default: the pass can dominate total runtime, and being the last thing to run before the final convergence check, anything it degrades is reported as a quality failure rather than a coarsening one.

Coarsen as far as the quality guarantee allows, instead of stopping at the target edge length. The pass then answers how few elements can hold this max energy, which is more aggressive than it sounds because the answer ignores how big the elements become; measured over the registered models it roughly doubles the cell reduction while raising max energy on none of them. On by default. Turned off, it leaves alone any edge already at or past the collapse threshold, since collapsing it only makes its neighbours longer. The sizing field is deliberately not applied either way: honouring it here would leave the pass unable to undo refinement that turned out to be unnecessary.

Cap on the coarsen/smooth alternation; the pass also stops as soon as a round accepts no collapse. A round does not exist to finish what the previous one started: within a round the collapse pass already runs to a fixed point, so repeating the collapse alone finds nothing. What a round adds is the global smoothing in between, which moves that fixed point. Returns decay fast, and the default of two carries the large majority of the coarsening for a fraction of what the later rounds would cost.
Ordinary whole-mesh smoothing passes run between coarsening rounds. This is what makes a second round worth running at all -- see coarsen_max_rounds -- so setting it to 0 collapses the rounds to one.

How far the local smoothing after each coarsening collapse reaches, in rings; the pass locks one ring wider than this. Deliberately 1 rather than TriWild's and TetWild's 2: a smaller ball perturbs less per collapse, so more collapses clear the offset's absolute coarsening bar.

Smoothing sweeps over the ring inside each candidate coarsening collapse, before its max energy is measured, so the collapse is judged on a relaxed neighbourhood rather than on the configuration it lands in. 0 by default: the ring is large enough that even two sweeps cost hundreds of nonlinear solves per candidate, and turning it off costs almost no cell reduction because the pass runs to a fixed point and finds another candidate instead. At 0 the only relaxation is the global smoothing between rounds, which has no per-operation accept test of its own -- see the forced quality veto in TetOptimizerMesh::coarsen_mesh().

Fire the sizing refinement when an iteration's improvement is small next to the distance the metric still has to cover: (prev - cur) <= stall_eps * (cur - target). 0 means only when it does not improve at all.

Iterations to skip after a sizing refinement before another may fire. Default 1, matching the tetwild component: the refined sizing needs one split/collapse round to act before the stall detector can fairly judge it. 0 allows one every iteration.
How many worst faces seed the refinement. 0 means every face above the filter threshold, which is TriWild's default.
Vertex rings grown around each seeded face before the sizing scalar is lowered.
Multiplicative reduction of the per-vertex sizing scalar per refinement.
Floor on the per-vertex sizing scalar.
Neighbouring sizing scalars may differ by at most this factor. The smoothing only ever lowers a scalar, spreading refinement outward. <= 1 disables it.
On a stall, also split each seeded face's longest edge once, bypassing the length gate and without touching the sizing field.

What the surviving vertex of a collapse keeps as its sizing scalar. true (the default): the smaller of the two, which is the shared engine's rule. false: its own scalar, restored after the base collapse. The min rule carries substantially more vertices and lengthens the placement loop where the front travels, because the offset's sizing follows a moving front and has to relax behind it, which a scalar that only ever falls cannot do.

The outer loop's budget, in turns, one turn being split, collapse and swap with smoothing after each, followed by the front test. An upper bound rather than a schedule -- exhausting it is a warning and not an error, because a front that needs more turns is a legitimate outcome to inspect.

l_min: the shortest edge the sizing field may ask for, in absolute units. If < 0, derived as min_edge_length_rel * target_distance -- tied to the offset distance rather than the bounding box, because the offset is what has to be resolved. This is a floor on REFINEMENT, so raising it makes the offset coarser (paper Fig. 18).

l_min as a multiple of target_distance, used when min_edge_length is negative. Negative (the default) derives it from the offset envelope epsilon, which is just offset_envelope (as a multiple of target_distance): TetWild's own floor (cap the sizing field below by the envelope eps, Sec 3.2) stated in the offset's units, since the front is only held to within eps and edges shorter than eps cannot buy fidelity. A pure anti-runaway rail, far below the chord length any tolerance actually needs.
Lower bound for the per-vertex sizing field (see max_sizing_scalar). Refinement stops once a vertex's sizing scalar reaches this fraction of the base target length.
Upper bound for the per-vertex sizing field, as a multiplier on the target edge length (splitting_l2/collapsing_l2). 1.0 means never coarser than the base target length.

Gradation cap for the sizing field: neighbouring vertices' sizing scalars may differ by at most this factor. After each refinement pass the refined vertices' lower sizing scalar is propagated outward -- monotone, only ever lowering a neighbour's scalar -- so the mesh does not jump straight from fine to coarse. <= 1 disables gradation. Only read when sizing_gradation_mode is 'ring'.

How a lowered sizing scalar spreads to the vertices around it, at every place the offset lowers the field (the sag rule, the stuck refine). 'ring' (the default): the base gradation_smooth_sizing -- walk outward over mesh neighbours, capping each neighbour at sizing_gradation times the scalar it came from, so the field grades by mesh rings and a fine seed in a coarse mesh drags a shell of rings down with it. 'distance': TetWild's adjust_sizing_field gradation -- walk outward from the seeds and multiply every vertex within R = 1.8 l of its nearest seed by the linear ramp 0.5 + 0.5 dist / R (halved next to a seed, untouched at R), stopping at R; the seeds keep the value they were just given and nothing outside the ball changes. The refinement then reaches a seed geometrically through the split pass (each split child takes the mean of its parents' scalars) instead of by rings, so a fine target stays local to the seed however coarse the mesh around it is.
Incident-cell count above which a vertex in a split edge's link accepts only one valence-increasing split per pass, or 0 to disable. Spreads refinement instead of letting it pile onto one vertex.

Bisections tried by the projected line search before it gives up on a vertex: the step along the Newton direction is halved this many times, each candidate projected onto the input, and the first that does not invert and lowers the worst incident element is taken.

After the projected line search gives up, revisit each candidate and bisect between the interpolated point and its projection this many times, taking the longest step toward the input that still does not invert and still lowers the worst element. Lets a vertex whose one-ring cannot tolerate a full projection still travel toward the input, instead of being refused every pass from the same place. 0 disables the pass.

The engine's smoothing veto (TetWild's, TriWild's, SimWild's smooth_quality_veto, which this key replaces in this component; a config that still sets that name is refused): a move of a NON-FRONT vertex is refused when the largest per-cell energy over its ring rises (tet_energy() in 3D, tri_energy() in 2D; for a vertex off the front that is w times the engine's cell quality, AMIPS^3 in 3D and AMIPS in 2D). Default true, TetWild's behaviour. Front vertices are switched by offset_front_smooth_veto instead. Measured 2026-09-28 on the cube (target 1e-2, tolerance 1e-4): with this and the front veto both off the loop converged in 6 turns serial (20876 faces, max AMIPS 7.68); the comparison with this on and the front veto off is the run 'mix' of the same day.

Whether a FRONT vertex's smoothing move is refused when the largest per-tet energy over its ring rises (TopoOffsetTetMesh::tet_energy(): w AMIPS^3 plus the offset terms of the front faces a band cell carries, w = offset_amips_weight; in 2D TopoOffsetTriMesh::tri_energy(), w AMIPS plus the front chords' terms); the front's twin of offset_smooth_veto, applied by the component after the solve. The smoother minimises the SUM of the ring's energy and the veto bounds its MAX, TetWild's structure; the per-pass line 'front veto: fired X of Y' reports the refusals. DEFAULT FALSE since 2026-09-30 (it was true from the same morning): on the 3x-subdivided simple models at target_distance_rel 0.1 (serial, all other defaults) the cube and the prism diverged with it on, while with it off all four (cube, prism, sphere, cylinder) converged; the sphere and cylinder converged either way in about the same time. With it on, the cube kept a handful of folded-over front vertices from the first turn that the loop never cleared. The case for it, measured on the cube outward at target_distance_rel 1e-2 / front_conv_rel 1e-4 (2026-09-29, serial): with the weight alone the band's max AMIPS reached 53; with this veto too, 15-19 (5 turns, 4874 faces). With all three defaults it refuses about 57% of front moves and the loop still converges. The veto needs the small weight: at w = 1, AMIPS^3 sets the ring's max, so a vertex 0.3 of the offset distance off, which has to move by about its tets' size, is refused (2026-09-28: the ring error stayed at 20-40x the bar and refinement doubled the faces every turn, 159382 faces at turn 7, no convergence). Switch it off when setting w = 1. Both dimensions read it.

The weight w of AMIPS in the per-tet energy, tet_energy = w AMIPS^3 + the offset terms of the front faces a band cell carries (each term 1 at the bar), and in the front smoother's objective (w times the ring's AMIPS^3 plus the offset terms of the vertex's front faces). The collapse and swap energy rules, the swap case search, their early halves on the AMIPS^3 lower bound, and the front smoothing veto all compare this one energy. DEFAULT 1e-4 since 2026-09-30: an AMIPS^3 of 1e4 weighs as much as one bar, so the offset terms decide the maxima the rules compare, and an operation or a front move cannot push a face over the bar for a shape gain; AMIPS still keeps the solve's tangential directions determined and still acts as a barrier at degenerate cells (MAX_ENERGY is never scaled). Measured 2026-09-29 at target_distance_rel 1e-2 / front_conv_rel 1e-4, with offset_front_smooth_veto and offset_collapse_changed_cells on, against w = 1 with both off: cube outward 20102 -> 4300 faces (serial, turn 6 both); sphere outward resolved at turn 4 instead of 12; all eight of Spencer's cases (cube, prism, cylinder, sphere; outward and inward) resolved at 10 threads in 1-5 turns; inward, the largest error over a dense sampling of the cube's front fell from 2.68 to 0.26 bars. The crossing counter (DEBUG_crossings) located the gain: on the cube the collapses' crossings of the bar fell from 1142 to 91, and front moves that pushed their own vertex over it from 76 to 0. Cost: the band's max AMIPS rises from 7-8 to 13-29. 1 is the 1:1 energy of 2026-09-28. Interior vertices and the interior smoothing veto compare AMIPS alone and are unaffected by the scale. In 2D the same weight multiplies AMIPS (the 2D engine's cell quality, where 3D's is AMIPS^3) in tri_energy and the 2D front smoother; the measurements above are 3D.

The collapse energy rule over the cells whose energy the collapse changes, instead of the whole rings. true (DEFAULT since 2026-09-30): after = the max of tet_energy over the survivor's ring without the cells of v2's ring whose energy is unchanged (a collapse moves no vertex, so an untouched cell changes only through a front face relabelled across it); before = the max over v1's ring and over those same changed cells of v2's ring. false: the max over the survivor's ring after may not exceed the max over the rings of v1 and v2 before -- so a cell of v2's ring that the collapse does not change can set the cap, and a changed face may rise up to it. true is strictly stronger: it refuses every collapse false refuses, and more. The early half keeps the whole-ring max, which bounds both. Measured 2026-09-29 on the cube outward (target_distance_rel 1e-2, front_conv_rel 1e-4, serial) with offset_amips_weight 1e-4: the weight alone let the band's max AMIPS reach 53; adding this rule alone brought it to 15-19 (4098 faces). At w = 1 it changed nothing on the cube. 2D and 3D (in 2D over the faces of the rings; see TopoOffsetTriMesh::collapse_edge_after()).

Log-only: after every operation pass and every smoothing pass, count the front vertices whose ring measure crossed the bar (from <= 1 to > 1, and back), plus new vertices already over it; inside the front smoother, classify each accepted move whose ring-measure crossing it caused as the moved vertex's own or a front neighbour's. Changes no result; costs an exit-measure evaluation per pass and a local one per front move. 2D and 3D.

Whether a collapse is refused when the largest per-tet energy over the survivor's ring after the collapse exceeds the largest before it -- over the cells the collapse changes by default, over both endpoints' whole rings when offset_collapse_changed_cells is false (TetWild's collapse rule, ties allowed, on the per-cell energy instead of AMIPS: tet_energy() in 3D, see TopoOffsetTetMesh::collapse_after_connectivity(); tri_energy() in 2D, see TopoOffsetTriMesh::collapse_edge_after()). False accepts every collapse the engine's other checks (inversion, envelopes, topology) allow: a debugging switch, since the energy comparison is the only quality rule a collapse has.

Whether a swap must strictly lower the largest per-tet energy over the cells it makes against the cells it removes (TetWild's swap rule, on the per-cell energy; in 3D tet_energy(), see swap_after_cells(), the 4-4 / 5-6 case search swap_edge_44_energy() and the face-swap gate; in 2D tri_energy(), see TopoOffsetTriMesh::swap_edge_after(), where the only swap is the interior edge flip). False: the case search still takes its lowest-energy case but no improvement is required, and the face swap and the after-hook accept every non-inverted result: a debugging switch, since this comparison is the only quality rule a swap has.

How smoothing places a surface vertex. 'projected': smooth with AMIPS alone as if interior, then walk back toward the start projecting each candidate onto the input; accept the first projected candidate that does not invert and strictly lowers the worst incident element, else do not move. Lands exactly on the input; no weights. 'exact': minimize w_amips * AMIPS + (1-w_amips) * (d/eps)^2 with the true region-wise Hessian of the distance to the piecewise-linear input; sliding is free where the input is flat, held at corners, constrained along edges and curve segments. Rests a w_amips-proportional distance off the input.

Relative weight of the AMIPS quality term against the envelope term during smoothing of envelope-held vertices (the engine's input-surface envelope term); the envelope weight is 1 - w_amips. The front objective does not read it, in 2D or 3D: AMIPS enters at offset_amips_weight and the offset term at 1 / (front_conv / target_distance)^2, i.e. in units of the tolerance -- the two parts of the per-cell energy.
Check after every operation pass that no element is inverted and no tracked-surface simplex left its envelope. Slow; for debugging.

Whether everything outside the offset band deforms when the optimization pushes it. 3D: true (the default): no envelope holds a region boundary other than the input complex's -- the held surfaces are the input complex boundary and the domain wall -- and every cell outside the band is plastic: stamped with its rest shape at the top of optimize_offset() and before every operation group, with smoothing carrying a rest-shape AMIPS term for those cells weighted like the smoother's own. The other regions' boundaries stay tracked faces, so the operations preserve their topology (no collapse across them, no surface flip across a junction), but nothing holds them in place. false: every region boundary is held as well, in the same single envelope. Either way the offset surface is held by nothing during the loop; only the frozen-front final pass holds it, to offset_envelope. A cell keeps its rest shape until an operation touches it; an accepted split, collapse or swap re-stamps the cells it changed. 2D: true drops the other regions' per-tag envelopes at the top of optimize_offset() and releases them, as before.
